content: Minimizer parameter tradeoffs: random-scheme density ~2/(w+1); smaller minimizer length m gives fewer, longer super-mers (more skew), each +2 in m multiplies bucket count x16 (4^m). Super-mers extend until the minimizer changes; boundaries occur exactly at minimizer changes and each k-mer window belongs to exactly one super-mer. Edge k-mers at read ends appear in only one window (selected with prob 1/w vs 2/(w+1)) - a balance issue, not correctness, for counting, since the minimizer is a pure function of the k-mer; parallel segment splitting must overlap segments by a full window to avoid missing boundary minimizers (Zheng minimizers review). Reads shorter than k+w-1 collapse to a single window. Sources: HKUST GPU counting thesis, PeerJ syncmers (Edgar), Zheng 2023 review, NSF GPU distributed counting paper.
